root_cause.text: The RISC-V IOMMU driver failed to issue mandatory IOTINVAL commands to invalidate TLB and context caches after updating Device Directory Table (DDT) or Process Directory Table (PDT) entries in `riscv_iommu_iodir_update()`.
root_cause.evidence: The patch introduces the `riscv_iommu_iodir_iotinval()` helper function to send IOTINVAL commands and inserts calls to this function immediately after DDT invalidation commands in `riscv_iommu_iodir_update()`, satisfying the requirements of Sections 6.3.1 and 6.3.2 of the RISC-V IOMMU specification.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add helper function to handle RISC-V IOMMU directory cache invalidation (IOTINVAL) after modifying DDT or PDT entries.
intent_record.what: Added a new static helper function `riscv_iommu_iodir_iotinval` that constructs and sends IOTINVAL commands based on the device context, process context, and IOHGATP configuration.
intent_record.how: Enables proper cache invalidation of the IOMMU directory and process directory tables by sending spec-compliant IOTINVAL commands with appropriate PSCID and GSCID parameters depending on whether virtualization or process-directory translation is active.

intent_record.intent_summary: Invalidate I/O translation cache during RISC-V IOMMU directory updates to prevent stale translations.
intent_record.what: Added a call to riscv_iommu_iodir_iotinval() with default parameters and an explanatory comment inside the riscv_iommu_iodir_update loop.
intent_record.how: Ensures that I/O translation cache invalidation is triggered during directory updates, preventing the use of stale translations before SVA and PASID features are fully integrated.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add IOTLB invalidation during RISC-V IOMMU directory updates to ensure TLB consistency.
intent_record.what: Added a call to riscv_iommu_iodir_iotinval with default parameters and an explanatory comment inside the device ID loop of riscv_iommu_iodir_update.
intent_record.how: Triggers IOTLB invalidation during directory updates to maintain TLB consistency, temporarily bypassing SVA and PASID features.
